subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: Test Data Management for APIs
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Test Data Management for APIs.

hook.text: A test creates a user, runs assertions, but never deletes it. After 1,000 runs, the database has 1,000 ghosts.

buildup.text: Leftover test data pollutes environments, skews results, and causes tests to interfere with each other.

discovery.text: Tests should create their own data, use it, and clean it up—or use a fresh database for each run.

twist.text: Shared test data between tests creates hidden dependencies. Deleting one record can cascade-fail others.

climax.text: Using unique identifiers and cleanup hooks, the test suite leaves the database exactly as it found it.

punchline.text: Own your test data. Create it. Use it. Clean it up.

quiz.question: Why should tests clean up their own data?
options: Leftover data causes interference and pollution
